reason: The text describes the Israelites being tested by God to obey His commandments regarding the Sabbath. When some among the people disobey and go out to gather manna on the seventh day (despite explicit instruction not to), they find nothing. God explicitly expresses frustration with the people's refusal to keep His commandments and laws ('How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?'). The consequence of their disobedience—finding no manna when gathering on the Sabbath—directly results from their own failure to follow God's instructions. Thus the negative outcome (suffering the consequence of finding no food) is explicitly tied to their own fault (willful disobedience).
